incidents.victim: FBI Recruitment Portal; Oracle PeopleSoft customers globally
incidents.vector: Exploited unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) via contractor system at Accenture to breach FBI jobs portal and dozens of additional organizations across higher education, healthcare, tech, agriculture, and government.
incidents.impact: Approximately 5,000 FBI employee records stolen including medical, psychiatric, and home address data; Boeing subsidiary Jeppesen ForeFlight and others extorted; $70 million extorted from victims across 2026; multiple arrests — Dutch national Pepijn van der Stap, Jordanian teen Saif Al-din Khader, and Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky (CYPFER/CyberSteward).

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure; Taiwanese utilities and universities; Japanese and Polish airports; multinational NGO
incidents.attacker: China — Integrity Technology Group, government-linked commercial contractor
incidents.vector: China-based contractor Integrity Technology Group enabled state-linked actors to deploy MicroScan automated vulnerability scanning, FishHub spear-phishing malware delivery, Mirai-variant IoT botnets, and living-off-the-land techniques to achieve persistent access across global targets.
incidents.impact: Confirmed victims include a South Carolina power company, airports in Japan and Poland, Taiwanese natural gas and power infrastructure, approximately 20 Taiwanese universities, and a multinational NGO; DOJ and FBI seized the MicroScan and FishHub toolsets on October 8 in a court-authorized operation — the second disruption of Integrity Tech in two years.

incidents.victim: Taiwan academic and policy research organizations
incidents.vector: AI-generated spear-phishing emails impersonating academic institutions and QR code phishing on modified event posters directed targets to adversary-in-the-middle infrastructure that intercepted Google credentials and MFA tokens in real time.
incidents.impact: Confirmed targets include Taiwan's National Chengchi University Institute of International Relations and the Taiwan European Union Centre; Google account credentials and MFA tokens harvested in real time; campaign active since mid-2026 and ongoing.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors
incidents.vector: MatchBoil dropper delivered via spear-phishing installs MatchWok, a custom C# backdoor that establishes covert persistent access; malware has been continuously updated to evade detection since 2024.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy organizations persistently compromised for intelligence collection; malware continuously refined with new obfuscation techniques; campaign active since 2024 and ongoing.

incidents.victim: International hotel guests and business travelers (CaptiveCrunch campaign)
incidents.vector: Compromised hotel guest Wi-Fi captive portal networks to intercept device code authentication flows, then delivered fake software updates containing persistent malware; also conducted Microsoft Teams-based IT support impersonation to execute PowerShell and move laterally to domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Intelligence operatives and government officials traveling through affected hotel networks had credentials and devices compromised; lateral movement to domain controllers observed; campaign is ongoing with no public victim count disclosed.

incidents.victim: Yoido Full Gospel Church; SaRang Church (South Korea)
incidents.vector: Attackers deployed web shells to gain administrator access and used previously leaked passwords plus application vulnerabilities to breach internal systems including SAP ERP software; AI tools were used to analyze vulnerabilities and automate lateral movement and data extraction.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 850,000 Yoido Full Gospel Church members and 89,000 SaRang Church members exfiltrated, plus HR records for 286 employees including payroll, financial records, and internal communications; attacks traced to August 2026 with infrastructure linked to an earlier US-based Christian content platform compromise.

incidents.victim: South Korean financial institutions (loan and mobile banking platforms)
incidents.vector: Attacker used ARTEX, a Chinese-developed open-source AI-assisted pentesting framework, augmented with commercial LLMs (DeepSeek, GLM-5.3, and Grok) to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation against South Korean banking platforms.
incidents.impact: Multiple South Korean banking platforms breached and customer data exfiltrated; CrowdStrike recovered the attacker's AI chat history and configuration files from a compromised attack infrastructure system — a rare forensic window into an AI-assisted attack; suspect linked to South China University of Technology.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (Axios npm, Mastra AI, Rust arrayref)
incidents.vector: Compromised widely-used open-source packages to deploy ChainDrop, a self-replicating npm worm that infected 400+ downstream packages; blockchain-based command-and-control (EtherHiding, TxDataHiding, NullReceiver protocols) makes infrastructure seizure ineffective.
incidents.impact: Over 400 npm packages infected via ChainDrop worm; developer credentials and cryptocurrency wallet keys stolen through the PolinRider campaign; blockchain C2 ensures resilience against law enforcement takedowns; ongoing infection spreading through npm dependency graph.

incidents.vector: Social engineering impersonated a trusted contact to steal one ASOS employee's login credentials; attackers used those credentials to access Snowflake cloud data environment and Simon AI marketing platform, then sent an unauthorized push notification to all ASOS mobile app users linking to an attacker-controlled Telegram channel.
incidents.impact: Approximately 17 million customer records potentially exposed including names, contact details, and account data; ASOS share price dropped approximately 13% on disclosure; attackers announced a 2-week hold before potential data release; investigation continuing.

incidents.victim: Iraqi critical infrastructure (telecom, aviation); Israeli entity
incidents.vector: Fake Dubai Airports IT job offers delivered via social engineering lured targets to install ShelbyLoader V2 malware; GitHub API used as command-and-control channel to blend with legitimate traffic and evade network detection.
incidents.impact: Iraqi telecommunications and aviation infrastructure persistently compromised for intelligence collection; credential harvesting also conducted against an Israeli entity between May and June 2026; campaign ongoing with no confirmed data exfiltration volumes disclosed.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway globally
incidents.vector: Two chained unauthenticated remote code execution zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, CVSS 9.5 each) exploited via DTLS protocol manipulation and command injection before vendor disclosure; web shells deployed for persistent access.
incidents.impact: Over 50,000 instances exposed globally; US-based organizations confirmed as early targets with infrastructure reconnaissance beginning August 21; mass exploitation accelerated post-disclosure; web shells enabling ongoing access on unpatched systems.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of three hot wallet layers at Singapore-based crypto exchange Bitget, draining liquidity pool funds held on standby for customer transactions.
incidents.impact: Over $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from Bitget hot wallets — the largest crypto heist of 2026; exchange remained operational but funds in the affected hot wallet layer were fully drained.

incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing system left military personnel records unauthenticated and accessible over the internet for approximately nine months; unauthorized parties accessed data during the exposure window.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased US military personnel exposed unencrypted, including names, Social Security numbers, and unit assignments; data accessible from October 2025 through July 2026; scope of who accessed the data remains under investigation.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against ATNS operational technology network providing weather data services to air traffic controllers; insider collaboration by an employee is suspected and under investigation.
incidents.impact: Attack targeted systems that, if fully disrupted, could have crippled domestic and international air traffic across 6% of the world's airspace; weather OT network taken offline; attack was stopped but investigation into insider involvement is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Social engineering compromised access to third-party-hosted business applications between June 3-8; attackers exfiltrated patient health data and sent an extortion demand requiring payment to prevent public disclosure.
incidents.impact: At least 360,000 patients across Texas, South Carolina, and California affected; stolen data includes names, addresses, insurance numbers, cardiac device serial numbers, and dates of cardiac monitoring service; company filed state breach notifications in October 2026.
